explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states or quickly implies this result. The theorem builds a p-subgroup T of Q ⊔ R that contains Q, with T ⊔ R = Q ⊔ R, and such that T ⊓ R is the image of a Sylow p-subgroup of R. I read the declaration list of Mathlib/GroupTheory/Sylow.lean and grepped Mathlib for Sylow lemmas involving ⊓, inf, subgroupOf or Normal. Mathlib has `IsPGroup.exists_le_sylow`, `Sylow.subtype` and `IsPGroup.le_sylow_of_normal`, but no lemma saying that a Sylow subgroup intersected with a normal subgroup is Sylow in that normal subgroup. The library's proof depends on its own lemma `normal_subgroup_image_sylow_intersection`, which has no Mathlib counterpart. It also needs several steps of subgroup bookkeeping (sup, map and subgroupOf manipulations). That is more than a one- or two-line derivation.
